exposure: Prolonged second stage of labour (>3 h with an epidural or >2 h without)
Second stage of labour within normal limits
outcome: Mode of delivery (Caesarean, spontaneous vaginal, instrumental)
Neonatal intensive care unit admissions > 72 h
cohort: The study included 55,309 primiparous women with term births of live singleton vertex fetuses from a tertiary medical center between 2005 and 2022.
finding: Prolonged second stage of labour was independently associated with a higher risk for composite adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Prolonged second stage of labour was associated with significantly higher rates of Caesarean and instrumental deliveries and lower rates of spontaneous vaginal deliveries.
